speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your husband is presenting with bizarre and agitated behavior; to ensure his safety and determine the cause, I need to begin by asking you a few specific questions. Can you describe exactly what he said or did that you found most concerning, and did he recognize you when he arrived?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the belief that the NSA is spying on and controlling his mind, along with his withdrawal over three months, suggests a significant psychotic process. To better understand the severity of his agitation and rule out medical causes, REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Thyroid_Stimulation_Hormone, and Urine_Tox_Screen. Can you tell me if he has experienced any hallucinations or if he has a history of similar episodes before?

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial metabolic and toxicological screens are normal, which helps rule out common medical mimics. Given his six weeks of delusions, one month of withdrawal, and a new focus on constructing a device to stop mind control, do you or he have a history of hearing voices or seeing things that others do not? Also, has he experienced any significant change in sleep patterns, such as needing very little sleep without feeling tired?

speaker: Patient
text: creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia, First Episode.

The patient presents with a 6-week history of paranoid delusions (mind control by NSA) and disorganized behavior (building a device), accompanied by 3 months of prodromal withdrawal. With normal medical screens and a lack of reported hallucinations or sleep disturbance yet, the clinical picture strongly supports a primary psychotic disorder, specifically schizophrenia.
